lessons.title: Scope Functions Overview
lessons.content: let, run, with, apply, also execute a block in an object's context, differing in this/it and return value. Real scenario: apply to configure an object, let to safely transform a nullable.

codeSnippets.code:
val user = User().apply { name = "Alice" }
val length = nullableName?.let { it.trim().length }

lessons.title: Inline Functions
lessons.content: Marking a higher-order function inline copies its body to the call site, eliminating lambda allocation and enabling non-local returns. Real scenario: performance-sensitive utility functions in hot paths.

lessons.title: crossinline
lessons.content: Marks a lambda passed into another execution context (like Runnable) where non-local return would be unsafe. Real scenario: passing a lambda into Handler.post from an inline utility.

lessons.title: noinline
lessons.content: Marks a lambda parameter to NOT be inlined, needed when it must be stored as a reference. Real scenario: an inline function executing one lambda immediately and storing another for later use.

lessons.title: Class Delegation (by)
lessons.content: The 'by' keyword delegates interface implementation to another object, giving composition without forwarding boilerplate. Real scenario: a decorator adding caching on top of a Repository.

codeSnippets.code: class CachingRepository(private val base: Repository) : Repository by base

lessons.title: Delegated Properties (by)
lessons.content: A property delegates its get/set logic to a separate object implementing getValue/setValue. Real scenario: a custom delegate transparently reading/writing to DataStore.

codeSnippets.code: var name: String by Delegates.observable("initial") { _, old, new -> println("$old -> $new") }

lessons.title: lazy Delegation
lessons.content: by lazy { } defers expensive initialization until first access, then caches the result, thread-safe by default. Real scenario: lazily initializing a heavyweight parser only if needed.

codeSnippets.code: val parser: JsonParser by lazy { JsonParser() }

lessons.title: Delegates.observable
lessons.content: Runs a callback on every property change, receiving old and new values. Real scenario: triggering a UI refresh whenever a settings value changes.

codeSnippets.code: var theme: String by Delegates.observable("light") { _, old, new -> if (old != new) applyTheme(new) }

lessons.title: Delegates.vetoable
lessons.content: Like observable, but the callback decides whether the change is accepted. Real scenario: a high-score property that vetoable rejects any decrease attempt on.

codeSnippets.code: var highScore: Int by Delegates.vetoable(0) { _, old, new -> new > old }

lessons.title: lateinit
lessons.content: lateinit var declares a non-null property initialized later, useful when a value can't be known at construction time. Real scenario: a ViewModel property injected by DI after construction.

lessons.title: lateinit vs lazy: When to Use Which
lessons.content: lateinit for var set externally; lazy for val computed once internally. Real scenario: lateinit for Android View Binding, lazy for an internally-computed expensive object.

codeSnippets.code:
lateinit var binding: ActivityMainBinding
val viewModel: MainViewModel by lazy { MainViewModel() }

lessons.title: Basic Reflection
lessons.content: kotlin.reflect lets code inspect classes/properties at runtime. Real scenario: a generic logging utility printing an object's class name and properties automatically.

lessons.title: Annotations
lessons.content: Annotations attach metadata that tools/frameworks read at compile or runtime. Real scenario: your Room @Entity and @Dao annotations generating database boilerplate at build time.

codeSnippets.code:
@Entity(tableName = "lessons")
data class LessonEntity(@PrimaryKey val id: String, val title: String)

lessons.title: Operator Overloading
lessons.content: Define custom behavior for operators on your own types via functions marked 'operator'. Real scenario: overloading + on a Money class so total = price1 + price2 reads naturally.

lessons.title: Destructuring Declarations
lessons.content: Unpacks an object's properties into separate variables using componentN(). Real scenario: unpacking a Pair, or unpacking Map entries directly in a for loop.

codeSnippets.code:
data class Point(val x: Int, val y: Int)
val (x, y) = Point(3, 4)

lessons.title: Contracts
lessons.content: The experimental contract { } block lets a function tell the compiler about its own effects, enabling smart casts based on custom validation. Real scenario: a custom isValidUser() check that smart-casts.

lessons.title: Smart Casts
lessons.content: The compiler auto-casts a variable after a check, only when it can prove the value can't change in between. Real scenario: understanding why var class properties often don't smart-cast reliably.

lessons.title: DSL Builders
lessons.content: Lambdas with receiver plus extension functions let you design fluent, type-safe configuration APIs. Real scenario: the mechanism behind Compose's UI tree and Gradle's build.gradle.kts.

lessons.title: Context Receivers (Experimental)
lessons.content: An evolving feature letting a function require an implicit context available in scope, without an explicit parameter everywhere. Real scenario: a function requiring an implicit Logger context.
